title: Rising labels: First qualifying slip
topics: Greedy choices, dynamic programming and backtracking
summary: For each index i, produce the greatest length of a strictly increasing subsequence that ends at readings[i]. Equal values cannot extend a subsequence. Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index.
descriptionMd:
A proofreader studies increasing label histories that must finish at each current reading. Sol needs the first qualifying slip while the courier waits at the door. Later matches must not jump ahead in the tray.

For each index i, produce the greatest length of a strictly increasing subsequence that ends at readings[i]. Equal values cannot extend a subsequence.

Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index.

Implement risingLabelsFirstQualifyingSlip(readings, k). Use k exactly where specified above.
unitIntro: Sequence DP with binary search. For each index i, produce the greatest length of a strictly increasing subsequence that ends at readings[i]. Equal values cannot extend a subsequence. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.

Target time O(n log n); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with sequence dp with binary search. What state describes the portion you have already processed?

For each index i, produce the greatest length of a strictly increasing subsequence that ends at readings[i]. Equal values cannot extend a subsequence. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.
Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index. Handle the empty derived sequence according to the stated return rule.
